channel.title: Chovy's Blog
channel.description: Tech, agentic coding, and whatever else I'm building. By Anthony "chovy" Ettinger.

item.title: What each feature actually costs me in AI
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: Five agents, five git worktrees, one command that reads the engines' own logs. Over 90 percent of a $228 day turned out to be cache reads, and a bug hunt cost 65 times what a short blog session did.

item.title: Our customers block ads, so we sell them in the terminal
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: Every product we ship is aimed at developers, and developers are the hardest audience on earth to buy. So we built the one ad format nobody else sells: a plain text unit you curl into an MOTD.

item.title: Two hours from idea to a live URL
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: I wanted a notification before my team played. Two hours later tipoffwatch.com was live. Why ESPN's free JSON made it possible, what the stack decisions actually cost, and the bugs that only showed up once real data hit it.

item.title: The AI storage pitch is a load balancing problem
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: I signed up for an F5 and Scality webinar about feeding GPUs from object storage, then read the technical writeup behind it. The interesting parts are hot spot avoidance, what erasure coding actually costs, and why post quantum TLS matters more than the handshake.

item.title: One token, zero scopes, and the .env I clobbered
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: Setting a single environment variable on a crawler meant picking a token with no permissions, and accidentally overwriting the .env I was only trying to read. Why secrets belong in a vault instead of a file, and how the logicsrc CLI does it.

item.title: Cloning takes a weekend, finding the 38% took months
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: I posted 'hire us or we'll clone your ass in a weekend' on LinkedIn. The cloning part is true and boring. Here is what a weekend does not buy, using two bugs I found in my own product yesterday.

item.title: The break and fix is the part worth watching
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: A Bluesky post said polished tutorials hide the friction. Here is this morning's friction: I shipped a near-black ad bar onto a blog that is black on white, and the fix turned into two palettes per creative and a tag that measures the page.

item.title: One writer, twelve workers, zero rows
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: My feed crawler stopped dead on SQLite write locks. It was not the 14GB database, the FTS triggers, the batch size or the quota. It was a dozen concurrent transactions fighting over a lock one of them could hold. The fix was a BullMQ queue with concurrency 1 on Bun.

item.title: I was too broke to buy ads, so I built my own ad network
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: I could never afford to buy advertising, so I built crawlproof.com/ads instead. Six weeks in it serves 59,012 impressions a month across 22 sites. Here are the real numbers, including the third of them that is my own server talking to itself.

item.title: Puzzle nights are up 151% and my team works alone
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: Axios says America is having a meetup explosion: puzzle competitions up 151%, mahjong up 94%, birding and silent book clubs. I run a fully remote shop, so here is what we are asking our team and our clients to do about it.
